tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main

/-!
# Access kernel: no active authority covers a leaf of its own holder

The auxiliary invariant `NoSelfLock` (not a clause of §57 of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`): no authority satisfies `SelfLock` (§63.8). It
holds initially (§47) and every kernel step keeps it from a `WF3` state (§49): `transfer` through
§63.8, `store` through §65.3, `alloc` because its new root covers only new leaves (§71), the other
steps because they move no holder onto a covered place (§60–§75 `ok` effects). Hence it holds on
every reachable state (§57, `reachable_noSelfLock`).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- `NoSelfLock` (auxiliary invariant, not a clause of §57): no authority is `SelfLock` (§63.8;
kept by §63.8 and §65.3, see also §88). -/
def NoSelfLock (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ x, ¬ SelfLock s x

/-- Introduction of `NoSelfLock` (§63.8). -/
theorem noSelfLock_intro {s : S3}
    (h : ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
      l ∈ y.footprint → l ∈ holderLeaves s y.holder → False) : NoSelfLock s := by
  intro x hx
  unfold SelfLock at hx
  cases hy : s.A[x]? with
  | none => rw [hy] at hx; exact hx
  | some y => rw [hy] at hx; obtain ⟨ya, l, hl, hh⟩ := hx; exact h x y l hy ya hl hh

/-- Elimination of `NoSelfLock` (§63.8). -/
theorem NoSelfLock.elim {s : S3} (h : NoSelfLock s) {x : Nat} {y : Authority} {l : Nat}
    (hy : s.A[x]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) (hl : l ∈ y.footprint)
    (hh : l ∈ holderLeaves s y.holder) : False :=
  h x (by unfold SelfLock; rw [hy]; exact ⟨ya, l, hl, hh⟩)

/-- A frame has no leaves (§63.8). -/
theorem not_mem_holderLeaves_frame {s : S3} {f l : Nat} : l ∉ holderLeaves s (.frame f) :=
  fun h => by simp [holderLeaves] at h

/-- `NoSelfLock` depends only on the places and the authorities (§38, §63.8). -/
theorem NoSelfLock.congr {s s' : S3} (h : NoSelfLock s) (hA : s'.A = s.A) (hP : s'.P = s.P) :
    NoSelfLock s' :=
  noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => by
    rw [hA] at hy
    exact h.elim hy ya hl (by unfold holderLeaves at hh ⊢; rw [hP] at hh; exact hh)

/-- An element of an appended list comes from one of the two parts (§42: authorities added by
`split`). -/
private theorem getElem?_append_cases {α : Type} {l E : List α} {x : Nat} {y : α}
    (h : (l ++ E)[x]? = some y) : l[x]? = some y ∨ y ∈ E := by
  by_cases hx : x < l.length
  · rw [List.getElem?_append_left hx] at h; exact .inl h
  · rw [List.getElem?_append_right (by omega)] at h; exact .inr (List.mem_of_getElem? h)

/-! ## The initial state (§47) -/

/-- The initial state satisfies `NoSelfLock` for a well-formed statics declaration (`StaticsOK`,
§47): the root authority of a root static is held by frame 0 or by its owning static, an earlier
static that is not a part of it (§40, §47). -/
theorem init_noSelfLock {statics : Statics} (hst : StaticsOK statics) :
    NoSelfLock (S3.init statics) := by
  have hw : WF3 (S3.init statics) := (init_kinv hst).1.1
  have hlen : (S3.init statics).P.length = statics.length := by simp [S3.init, shapeP]
  refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
  simp only [S3.init, List.getElem?_map] at hy
  obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 hy
  have hmem := List.mem_of_getElem? hi
  simp only [rootIdx, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, Option.isNone_iff_eq_none] at hmem
  obtain ⟨hil, hpn⟩ := hmem
  have hroot : RootPlace (S3.init statics).P i := by
    refine ⟨by rw [hlen]; simpa using hil, ?_⟩
    simp only [parentOf, S3.init, shapeP, List.nil_append, List.getElem?_map,
      List.getElem?_range hil, Option.map_some, Option.bind_some]
    simpa using hpn
  simp only [shapeOwner] at hh
  split at hh
  · rename_i o ho
    have hoi : o < i := by
      have := (hst i (List.mem_range.2 hil)).2
      rw [ho] at this; have := this.2; omega
    obtain ⟨r, hr, hor⟩ := exists_rootPlace hw (o + 1) o (Nat.lt_succ_self o)
      (by rw [hlen]; simp at hil; omega)
    have hlr := footprint_sub hw hor hh
    obtain rfl := rootOf_unique hr hroot (mem_footprint.1 hlr).2.2 (mem_footprint.1 hl).2.2
    have := Frames.partOf_le hor; omega
  · exact not_mem_holderLeaves_frame hh

/-! ## Preservation by every step (§60–§75) -/

/-- Every kernel step keeps `NoSelfLock` from a `WF3` state (§49.8: holders of active authorities
are live): `derive`, `split` and `enterFrame` add frame-held authorities (§60, §61, §72);
`release`, `exitFrame`, `endUse`, `free` only deactivate, reanchor or keep authorities (§62, §73,
§69, §70); `transfer` is guarded by §63.8 and keeps footprints (§63); `store` by §65.3; the new
root of `alloc` covers only new leaves, its owner only former ones (§71); the remaining steps
change neither places nor authorities (§64, §66–§68, §74, §75). -/
theorem kstep_preserves_noSelfLock {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (hns : NoSelfLock s)
    (h : KStep k s s') : NoSelfLock s' := by
  cases h with
  | derive h =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
    rcases addAuth_get hy with ⟨-, hy⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
    · exact hns.elim hy ya hl hh
    · exact not_mem_holderLeaves_frame hh
  | split h =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
    rcases getElem?_append_cases hy with hy | hy
    · exact hns.elim hy ya hl hh
    · obtain ⟨r, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hy; exact not_mem_holderLeaves_frame hh
  | release h =>
    rename_i a
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    cases hx₀ : s.A[a]? with
    | none => simp only [releaseEff, hx₀]; exact hns
    | some x₀ =>
      rw [releaseEff_eq hx₀]
      refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
      simp only [set_get (lt_of_getElem? hx₀)] at hy
      split at hy
      · cases hy; cases ya
      · exact hns.elim hy ya hl hh
  | transfer h =>
    rename_i src dst
    obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
    have hy' := hy
    rw [transfer_A_get] at hy'
    obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, e⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 hy'
    by_cases hin : heldIn s.P src y₀.holder
    · refine hpre.noSelfLock x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy₀)) (by rw [hy₀]; exact hin) ?_
      unfold SelfLock; rw [hy]; exact ⟨ya, l, hl, hh⟩
    · simp only [hin, ↓reduceIte] at e; subst e
      refine hns.elim hy₀ ya hl ?_
      cases hho : y₀.holder with
      | frame f => rw [hho] at hh; exact absurd hh not_mem_holderLeaves_frame
      | place q =>
        rw [hho] at hh
        show l ∈ footprint s.P q
        rw [← transfer_footprint s src dst q]; exact hh
  | depend h =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact hns.congr rfl rfl
  | enter h =>
    rename_i ps ls
    obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
    rcases Frames.enter_get hy with ⟨-, y₀, hy₀, e⟩ | ⟨-, i, -, rfl⟩
    · split at e
      · subst e; exact not_mem_holderLeaves_frame hh
      · subst e
        cases hho : y.holder with
        | frame f => rw [hho] at hh; exact not_mem_holderLeaves_frame hh
        | place q =>
          rw [hho] at hh
          have hu : s.Usable q := by have := hw.holders x y hy₀ ya; rw [hho] at this; exact this
          refine hns.elim hy₀ ya hl ?_
          rw [hho]; exact (Frames.enter_footprint_old hpre.localsOK hu.lt l).1 hh
    · exact not_mem_holderLeaves_frame hh
  | exit h =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
    obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, rfl⟩ := Frames.exit_get hy
    obtain ⟨-, hf, hh'⟩ := Frames.exitG_same s s.F.tail x y₀
    rw [hf] at hl; rw [hh'] at hh
    exact hns.elim hy₀ (Frames.exitG_active' hy₀ ya) hl hh
  | read h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact hns
  | write h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact hns.congr rfl rfl
  | writeShared h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact hns.congr rfl rfl
  | pin h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact hns.congr rfl rfl
  | unpin h => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact hns.congr rfl rfl
  | endUse h =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    exact noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh =>
      hns.elim (EndFree.endUse_active hy ya).1 ya hl hh
  | free h =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    exact noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh =>
      hns.elim (EndFree.free_active hy ya).1 ya hl hh
  | alloc h =>
    cases h with
    | ok hst _ =>
      refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
      rcases Alloc.allocA_get hst hy with ⟨-, hy₀⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
      · cases hho : y.holder with
        | frame f => rw [hho] at hh; exact not_mem_holderLeaves_frame hh
        | place q =>
          rw [hho] at hh
          have hu : s.Usable q := by have := hw.holders x y hy₀ ya; rw [hho] at this; exact this
          refine hns.elim hy₀ ya hl ?_
          rw [hho]; exact (Alloc.footprint_old hst.shapeOK hu.lt l).1 hh
      · have h1 := Alloc.fp_new_ge hl
        have h2 := (Alloc.footprint_old hst.shapeOK hst.ownerUsable.lt l).1 hh
        have := (mem_footprint.1 h2).1; omega
  | store h =>
    rename_i a p
    obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    cases hy₁ : s.A[a]? with
    | none => simp only [storeEff, hy₁]; exact hns
    | some y₁ =>
      have heq : storeEff s a p = { s with
          A := s.A.set a { y₁ with holder := .place p }
          D := fun q => if q = p then s.D p ++ [a] else s.D q
          I := fun l => if l = p then .init else s.I l } := by
        simp only [storeEff, hy₁]
      rw [heq]
      refine noSelfLock_intro fun x y l hy ya hl hh => ?_
      simp only [set_get (lt_of_getElem? hy₁)] at hy
      split at hy
      · cases hy
        exact (hpre.noCover l (by simp only [S3.afp, hy₁]; exact hl)).1 hh
      · exact hns.elim hy ya hl hh

/-! ## Reachable states (§57) -/

/-- `NoSelfLock` (auxiliary invariant, not a clause of §57; §63.8, §65.3) holds on every state
reachable from `S3.init statics`, under `DDSound` (§80, through `reachable_kinv`, which gives
`WF3`) and `StaticsOK` (§47). -/
theorem reachable_noSelfLock {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hst : StaticsOK statics) (h : Reachable k statics s) : NoSelfLock s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact init_noSelfLock hst
  | step hr h ih => exact kstep_preserves_noSelfLock (reachable_kinv hdd hst hr).1 ih h

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

    90	  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, e⟩ := (transfer_skel s src dst).get hy

   174	the clause is kept in `TransferPre`): on a state reachable under `DDSound` (§80) from well-formed
   175	statics (§47), the `Modify` right over `src` (§63.1, `TransferPre.srcRight`) implies the
   176	derived-outside check of §63.4 (`TransferPre.noOutsideDerived`), for an authority grounding that
   177	right; so that check never rejects a `transfer` by itself on a reachable state. -/
   178	theorem reachable_noOutsideDerived_of_right {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} {src : Nat}
   179	    (hdd : DDSound k) (hst : StaticsOK statics) (hr : Reachable k statics s)

   181	    ∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify src g ∧
   182	      ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ActiveDerivedOutside s src j → RightChain s g j := by

   185	  cases hy : s.A[j]? with
   186	  | none => simp only [ActiveDerivedOutside, hy, OptP] at hj

   188	    simp only [ActiveDerivedOutside, hy, OptP] at hj

   190	    exact grounds_cover_rightChain (reachable_kinv hdd hst hr).2.1.1.1 ⟨hgr, hex, hall⟩ hy ya hl
   191	      hlq
   192	
   193	namespace TransferSourceWitness
   194

   196	
   197	/-- The state after `transfer(0, 1)` from `S3.init st` (§47, §63 `ok` effect): leaf 0 `Moved`,
   198	leaf 1 `Init`. -/
   199	def t1 : S3 := transferEff s0 0 1
   200	
   201	/-- Writes through the grounding authority itself are accepted on a moved source leaf (decision
   202	Q17, validated 2026-11-06; §63.4, §67, §68, §41, §53): under `K0` (`DDSound`, §80) and the
   203	well-formed statics `st` (§47), `S3.init st` is reachable, `transfer(0, 1)` is accepted, root
   204	authority 0 grounds the `Modify` right over place 0, leaf 0 is a `Moved` source leaf afterwards,

   207	write through the grounding authority itself is a permitted re-initialization of the `Moved`
   208	leaf. -/
   209	theorem write_through_ground_accepted : DDSound K0 ∧ StaticsOK st ∧ Reachable K0 st s0 ∧
   210	    TransferStep K0 0 1 s0 (.ok t1) ∧ Grounds s0 .modify 0 0 ∧ 0 ∈ footprint t1.P 0 ∧
   211	    t1.I 0 = .moved ∧ Write3Step 0 [0] t1 (.ok (write3Eff t1 [0])) ∧
   212	    WriteSharedStep K0 0 [0] t1 (.ok (write3Eff t1 [0])) ∧

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations (O9–O11) do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is an active derived or root authority, and `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` holds; its origin chain and anchors are valid: every authority of its origin chain, its effective anchor included, is active.
2. The leaves of `region` exist and belong to the footprint of `source`; `mode` does not exceed the available effective right on these leaves.
3. The addition preserves exclusivity I1: no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible with the derived right, and already-active descendants are respected.
4. The new holding frame is the live current frame. The admissible state's footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true.

**`ok` effect:** A new active authority with fresh identity, origin `source`, requested mode and footprint, and held by the current frame is added. The source remains active; its effective modes are recomputed per leaf. No storage or place anchor is created. Multiple compatible observations remain permitted. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights

These transitions govern value consumption and the controlled movement of their dependencies. A valid transition can neither create an additional permission nor discard a surviving anchor.

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved. No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check. Authorities held by parts of `source` are transferred with the value and are controlled by §63.8.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
9. **Destination usability:** `destination` is usable in the resulting state.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor

**Preconditions**

1. `result` is a usable place over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
2. `anchor` designates an active, valid authority representing a real dependency of the relevant rights or storage; a declared dependency cannot extend an origin's lifetime.
3. Existing anchors are preserved and the addition respects `AnchorOrder`: the effective anchor's frame is the frame of `result` or an ancestor thereof.
4. Every dependency carried by a contained value remains represented in the transitive obligations of its container.

**`ok` effect:** `anchor` is added to `D(result)`; the container's transitive dependencies account for it. No additional access right is created. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

A safe interface must declare dependencies covering those actually required by its implementation; the annotation itself is not presumed true. An unsafe abstraction bears the obligations of its contract.

## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active, **derived**, and held by the current frame; a root authority can never be stored by `store`.
2. `target` is a usable **leaf** under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It holds no other **active** authority. Its data already being `Init` does not by itself prohibit the operation.
3. The stored authority covers neither a leaf of `target` nor the leaves of storage transitively owned by it.
4. The effective anchor of `authority` respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`; other dependencies are preserved.
5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.

**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.

# X. Reading, Writing, and Initialization

A leaf's initialization state and the effective right to access it are two distinct conditions.

## 66. O9 — Safe Reading of Regions

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf being read belongs to a usable place and is `Init`.
2. `access` is an authority exercisable in `Observe` mode over the region; its **effective** mode actually permits observation of each leaf being read.
3. Required anchors are valid, and the type and storage contract permits this read.

**`ok` effect:** The logical read succeeds, without modifying `F`, `P`, `I`, `A`, `D`, or arena entries. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

`Moved` and `Uninit` cannot be read. This definition does not replace concrete representation and pointer checks of the elementary memory machine.

## 67. O10 — Ordinary Write

**Preconditions**

1. Targeted leaves belong to usable places, and `access` is exercisable in `Modify` mode with **effective** `Modify` right over each leaf.
2. No incompatible ordinary authority holds an incompatible effective mode over the written leaves (I1).
3. Anchors and constraints of the relevant types, storage, and abstractions remain valid.

**`ok` effect:** The logical write sets the actually written leaves to `Init` and does not modify authorities or their anchors. An unwritten leaf does not become `Init` by this effect. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 68. O11 — Write Under Shared Mutation

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf in the region is usable and declared `K.SharedMutable`.
2. `access` is exercisable in a mode **at least** `Observe` and has a present effective mode on every leaf, either `Observe` or `Modify`; exercising an authority without an effective mode is insufficient.
3. Dependencies are valid and the particular shared-mutation discipline guaranteed by `K.SharedMutable` applies.

**`ok` effect:** Actually written leaves become `Init`; authorities and their structural exclusivity I1 do not change. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

`writeShared` may update metadata under an `Observe` authority when the contract permits. Stability of observed contents is not automatically guaranteed, and this kernel **does not prove** the absence of data races: that requires the concurrency model's guarantees.

# XI. End of Use, Deallocation, and Allocation

The logical end of a value does not necessarily entail deallocation of its storage. The following operations treat initialization, ownership, and physical release separately.

## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from this check. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (held by `place` or by a place dying with it, transitively owned storage included) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from the check on active derivatives. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (an authority of the released region, its root included, or an authority whose holder dies) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root

**Static preconditions**

1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
2. The provider is a usable place, and **all leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.

**Outcomes**

- `reject`: a static precondition does not hold;
- `fail`: static preconditions hold, but `K.Satisfiable(provider,shape,s)` is false in the state under consideration; **no state change**;
- `ok(s')`: creation of a **new storage root** with fresh identity, owned by `owner`; its leaves start `Uninit`, its new root `Modify` authority with no origin is held by `owner`; provider metadata is updated only in accordance with its modification rights.

Allocation success depends on the provider's state: it does not constitute a right to invent physical memory. Any realization of this operation must satisfy the `AllocStep` relation defined by the rules of Sections 9 and 13.

# XII. Call Frames and Return of Authorities

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

(hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (ha : y.active = true) (hm : m.le y.mode)
    (hf : y.holder = .frame s.top) : exR s m E a = true := by
  unfold exR; rw [hy]; simp [ha, hm, hf]

/-- The place-held case of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
theorem exR_held {s : S3} {m : Mode} {E : Nat → Bool} {a p b : Nat} {y : Authority}
    (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (ha : y.active = true) (hm : m.le y.mode) (hp : y.holder = .place p)
    (hb : b < s.A.length) (hc : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m)
    (hE : E b = true) : exR s m E a = true := by
  simp only [exR, hy, ha, hp, Bool.true_and, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq,
    List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
  exact ⟨hm, b, hb, hc, hE⟩

/-- `ExercisableAt` is computed by `|A| + 1` steps of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
theorem exercisableAt_iff {s : S3} {a : Nat} {m : Mode} :
    s.ExercisableAt a m ↔ kiter (exR s m) (s.A.length + 1) a = true := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, exercisableAt_of_kiter s m _ a⟩
  induction h with
  | base hy ha hm hf => exact exR_base hy ha hm hf
  | held hy ha hm hp hb hc ih =>
    rw [← kiter_fix (exR_rule s _)]
    have hb' := kiter_bound (exR_rule s _) _ _ ih
    exact exR_held hy ha hm hp hb' hc ih

/-- Decidability of `ExercisableAt` (§43). -/
instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (m : Mode) : Decidable (s.ExercisableAt a m) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ exercisableAt_iff.symm

/-- `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43): the current frame has an authority exercisable at `m` whose
effective mode permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
def HasRight (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.ExercisableAt a m ∧
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s a l) m

/-- Decidability of `HasRight` (§43). -/
instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Decidable (HasRight s m q) := by
  unfold HasRight; infer_instance

/-- Authority `g` grounds the right `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43; §63.4, §69.2, §70.3: "the
exercisable authority on which that right rests"): it is exercisable at `m` and its effective mode
permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
def Grounds (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Prop :=
  g ∈ List.range s.A.length ∧ s.ExercisableAt g m ∧
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s g l) m

/-- Decidability of `Grounds` (§63.4, §69.2, §70.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Decidable (Grounds s m q g) := by
  unfold Grounds; infer_instance

/-- Authority `j` is the grounding authority `g` or belongs to its origin chain (§63.4, §69.2,
§70.3: "the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain"). -/
def RightChain (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Prop := j = g ∨ j ∈ s.ancs g

/-- Decidability of `RightChain` (§63.4, §69.2, §70.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Decidable (RightChain s g j) := by
  unfold RightChain; infer_instance

/-! ## Dependencies and anchors (§44) -/

/-- Anchors of the value at `q`, inherited from its parts (§44: dependencies of contained values
are accounted for transitively). -/
  ∀ z ∈ List.range P.length, partOf P z dst →
    ∃ r ∈ List.range P.length, partOf P r src ∧ corr P src dst r = some z

/-- Decidability of `SameShape` (§63.2). -/
instance (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) : Decidable (SameShape P src dst) := by
  unfold SameShape; infer_instance

/-- Holder within the value at `q` (§63, §69, §70): `q` or one of its parts. -/
def heldIn (P : List Place) (q : Nat) : Holder → Prop
  | .place r => partOf P r q
  | .frame _ => False

/-- Decidability of `heldIn` (§63). -/
instance (P : List Place) (q : Nat) (h : Holder) : Decidable (heldIn P q h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold heldIn <;> infer_instance

/-- Holder `h` after the transfer of `src` to `dst` (§63, `ok` effect): part `r` of `src` becomes
`corr(r)`. Applied to holders within `src` only. -/
def mvTo (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) : Holder → Holder
  | .place r => .place ((corr P src dst r).getD dst)
  | .frame f => .frame f

/-- Anchors moved onto place `q` by the transfer (§63, `ok` effect, fourth item): those of every
part `r` of `src` with `corr(r) = q`. -/
def movedTo (s : S3) (src dst q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun r =>
    decide (partOf s.P r src ∧ corr s.P src dst r = some q)).flatMap s.D

/-- Effect of `transfer(source, destination)` (§63, `ok` effect): source leaves `Moved`,
destination leaves `Init`; authorities held by part `r` of `src`, and places owned by `r`, move
to `corr(r)`; the anchors of `r` follow `corr(r)`. -/
def transferEff (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    P := s.P.map fun pl =>
      if heldIn s.P src pl.owner then { pl with owner := mvTo s.P src dst pl.owner } else pl
    I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P dst then .init
      else if l ∈ footprint s.P src then .moved else s.I l
    D := fun q => if partOf s.P q src then [] else s.D q ++ movedTo s src dst q
    A := s.A.map fun y =>
      if heldIn s.P src y.holder then { y with holder := mvTo s.P src dst y.holder } else y }

/-- Active derived authority covering a leaf of `src` and not held within it (§63.4). -/
def ActiveDerivedOutside (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P src y.holder ∧
    ∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P src) False

/-- Decidability of `ActiveDerivedOutside` (§63.4). -/
instance (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Decidable (ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) := by
  unfold ActiveDerivedOutside; infer_instance

/-- The holder moves with the value at `src` (§63.6, §63.7): a part of `src` or storage it owns,
transitively. -/
def HolderMoves (s : S3) (src : Nat) : Holder → Prop
  | .place p => partOf s.P p src ∨ OwnedIn s.P src p
  | .frame _ => False

/-- Decidability of `HolderMoves` (§63.7). -/
instance (s : S3) (src : Nat) (h : Holder) : Decidable (HolderMoves s src h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold HolderMoves <;> infer_instance

/-- Authority `x` is a moved held authority (§63.7): its holder moves with the value at `src`. -/
def AnchorMoves (s : S3) (src x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => HolderMoves s src y.holder) False

/-- Decidability of `AnchorMoves` (§63.7). -/
instance (s : S3) (src x : Nat) : Decidable (AnchorMoves s src x) := by
  unfold AnchorMoves; infer_instance

/-- Dependencies of the usable places following the value at `src` (§63.6): the anchors of its
parts and of the usable storage it owns, transitively. -/
def movedDeps (s : S3) (src : Nat) : List Nat :=
  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun q =>
    decide (partOf s.P q src ∨ (OwnedIn s.P src q ∧ s.Usable q))).flatMap s.D

/-- Leaves of a holder (§63.8): those of a place, none for a frame. -/
def holderLeaves (s : S3) : Holder → List Nat
  | .place p => footprint s.P p
  | .frame _ => []

/-- Authority `a` is active and covers a leaf of its own holder (§63.8). -/
def SelfLock (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ ∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ holderLeaves s y.holder) False

/-- Decidability of `SelfLock` (§63.8). -/
instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Decidable (SelfLock s a) := by unfold SelfLock; infer_instance

/-- Local self-blocking prevention (§63.8): no authority held before the step within `src` covers,
in the resulting state, a leaf of its new holder `corr(r)`. -/
def NoLocalSelfLock (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => heldIn s.P src y.holder) False →
    ¬ SelfLock (transferEff s src dst) j

/-- Decidability of `NoLocalSelfLock` (§63.8). -/
instance (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Decidable (NoLocalSelfLock s src dst) := by
  unfold NoLocalSelfLock; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `transfer` (§63). -/
structure TransferPre (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §63.1: `source` is usable. -/
  srcUsable : s.Usable src
  /-- §63.1: `destination` is usable. -/
  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
  /-- §63.1: exercisable `Modify` over the source. -/
  srcRight : HasRight s .modify src
  /-- §63.1: exercisable `Modify` over the destination. -/
  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
  /-- §63.2: same shape of ordered subtrees. -/
  sameShape : SameShape s.P src dst
  /-- §63.3: all source leaves are `Init`. -/
  srcInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init
  /-- §63.3: no destination leaf is `Init`. -/
  dstNotInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init
  /-- §63.3: source and destination footprints are disjoint. -/
  disjoint : ¬ overlap s.P src dst
  /-- §63.4: no active derived authority covers a source leaf from outside the source, except the
  authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over the source: some authority
  grounding that right and its origin chain. -/
  noOutsideDerived : ∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify src g ∧
    ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ActiveDerivedOutside s src j → RightChain s g j
  /-- §63.5: no in-place source leaf is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false
  /-- §63.6: dependencies of the usable places following the value are valid. -/
  depsValid : ∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src, s.Active x
  /-- §63.6: `AnchorOrder` in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrder : AnchorOrder (transferEff s src dst)
  /-- §63.7: every moved held authority satisfies `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : ∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length, AnchorMoves s src x →
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
      OptP ((transferEff s src dst).A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
        EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)) True
  /-- §63.8: local self-blocking prevention. -/
  noSelfLock : NoLocalSelfLock s src dst
  /-- §63.9: `destination` is usable in the resulting state. -/
  dstUsableAfter : (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `transfer` (§63). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (TransferPre k s src dst) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable src ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify src ∧

## Summary

Reference formalization (Lean 4, `formal/`) of the ERN memory model, rebuilt on
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` after the arbitrations Q1–Q28 of the v0 blocking report and
their two follow-ups, then corrected after the Codex review of `e3339338` (owner decisions of
2026-11-06, Q17 and H49 validated). `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` is unchanged.

Modules: `MemoryModel/Machine` (Part III), `MemoryModel/Access/*` (Parts IV–XIII, XV–XVI), `MemoryModel/Arena`
(Part XIV), `MemoryModel/Refinement` and `RefinementArena` (§82), `Access/TransferSource` (Q17),
`Access/Statics` and `Access/Rename/*` (`StaticsOK` (a) and (b)), `Lib/HandlePool` and `Lib/DataStack`
(non-normative library contracts), `Corpus/*` (test modules, imported by no model module).

## Corrections after the Codex review of `e3339338` (owner decisions of 2026-11-06)

| Point | Commit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Spec line 29 | `df96b50` | aligned with line 3 ("corrective candidate, not yet validated") |
| 2. Q3, `freeSlot` as a kernel write | `5b24f20` | (a), (b), (c) proved; `meta_write_not_identity` extended to an accepted `freeSlot` (conforming case) |
| 3. Q17/W2 (validated) | `c25a219`, `17e5d65` | (a) proved; (b) proved for reads and strict ancestors, false for writes through the grounding authority itself (open point 1); W2 restated, not reclassified |
| 4. H49 (validated) | `17e5d65` | witnesses kept; I2 justification checked (`¬ I2` of both v0 effects) |
| 5. StaticsOK (a), (b) | `8775ffb`, `5ff52b5` | (a) proved with its converse; (b) proved as a kernel bisimulation |
| 6. §63.4 cross-reference | `df96b50` | one sentence pointing to §63.8, no semantic change |

## Spec v0.1 (commit `edbb7a3`, alone)

`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` is v0 with the header "Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate,
not yet validated" and the list of modified clauses: §36 (Q13), §40 (Q15), §47 (Q8), §51 and §60.1 (Q9/Q26),
§57 I5 (Q16), §59 (Q14), §63.4, §69.2 and §70.3 (Q9 and Q3 follow-ups: grounding exemption and kept-descendant
rule), §63.9 (Q1), §71.2 (Q24), §74 and §75 (B#45), §76.6 (Q2), §78.3 (Q7), §82.2 (Q18), §86 (Q6).

Corrections of 2026-11-06 (commit `df96b50`, only these two sentences): the "Validation and Revision
Procedure" now states the status of line 3 (corrective candidate, not yet validated); §63.4 gains one
cross-reference sentence (authorities held by parts of `source` are transferred with the value and
controlled by §63.8), with no semantic change.

## Local contracts (non-normative)

**HandlePool v0.5** = HandlePool v0.4 annex D with:
- HP5-1 (Q3, as decided on 2026-11-06): `freeSlot` is one kernel `write` (§67) of the metadata leaves of
  the pool, then the abstract update (entry free, generation + 1); no `endUse` effect. The metadata
  leaves are the leaves of the pool value, the place holding `internal` (`metaLeaves`); the decision does
  not name them, this is the reading taken (basis: §36 and HP5-3). Preconditions: administration right (live pool, `MetaRight`, §36), valid handle, no leaf
  of the entry `Init`.
- HP5-1' (Q3, second follow-up): no active strict descendant of this pool's `internal` covers the entry
  (replaces "derived from a companion"; covers §73 reanchoring onto `internal`). A pool nested in an entry
  blocks freeing that entry; the parent pool's authorities do not block the nested pool's `freeSlot`.
- HP5-1'' (Q5 extended to `freeSlot`): missing pool `reject`; invalid handle `fail` (a dead pool's handle is
  stale); then `reject` without the right; then `reject` on the content condition.
- HP5-2, HP5-3: the two mandatory proofs of Q3 (below).
- HP5-4 (Q4): D.2, D.3 and D.4 (3) per pool (the slot's pool); nested pools allowed.
- HP5-5 (Q5): handle validation precedes the right check in `resolve` and `resolveMany`: `fail`.
- HP5-6 (Q12): a handle of a free entry is stale: `fail`.
- HP5-7 (Q4): every library step is, on the kernel side, a sequence of accepted kernel steps O1–O16
  (`freeSlot`: one `write`, `pstep_kernel`); the kernel guarantees hold on the whole state
  (`kernel_guarantee`).
- Retired with the v0.4 `freeSlot`: `pool_freeSlot_ends_content`, the content-end machinery and the v0.4
  literal D.2/D.4 refutation witnesses.

**DS-v2** = DS-v1 with:
- DS2-1 (Q11 d): `mark` requires `AdminRight`, else `reject`.
- DS2-2 (Q11 e): `grow` stores the new block authority into the place currently holding the block authority.
- DS2-3 (Q28 c): a dead stack invalidates its marks: `rewind` is `fail`.
- DS2-4 (DS-R1): "a cell above m" is every cell at a position `≥ m.top`.
- DS2-5 (DS-R4): `grow` with `extra = 0` is `ok` (in-place reissue of the same region).
- DS2-6 (DS-R3): `rewind` on a missing stack index is `fail`.
- DS-v1 items now decided: push without room `fail` (Q11 a); `grow` of a non-block `reject` (Q11 b); §76.5
  applies to `newStack` (Q11 c); dead or foreign mark `fail` before the right (Q11 f); §36 applies to `rewind`
  (Q27 a).

## Guarantees asked by the arbitration, on reachable states, without extra non-normative hypothesis

Hypotheses used: `DDSound` (§80) and `StaticsOK` (§47). `StaticsOK` is a representation of §47/§49 (the
order of identifiers, §49 last paragraph), justified by StaticsOK (a) and (b) below.
- Q1: `Access.reachable_kinv` (§57 on reachable states, transfer no longer excepted);
  `Access.reachable_cycle_rejected` (the v0 ownership-cycle run is rejected by §63.9). Auxiliaries `KAux` and
  `HeldAnchored` are proved initially and preserved by every step (`reachable_inv`).
- Q3 (1): `Lib.HandlePool.Witness.freeSlot_after_transfer`: from `PState.init`, `newPool`, `allocSlot`,
  `resolve` Modify, `write`, `transfer` to a local of the same shape (created by `enterFrame`), `unresolve`,
  `freeSlot` accepted, with `internal` derived.
- Q3 (2): `Lib.HandlePool.freeSlot_meta_write`: on every library-reachable state, for a pool with `AdminRight`,
  the kernel `write` of the pool value through the authority grounding `MetaRight` is accepted.
- Q3 (decision of 2026-11-06), `freeSlot` realized by that write: (a) `freeSlot_meta_leaves` (the metadata
  leaves are exactly the leaves of the pool value; the write is accepted through the authority grounding
  the right, `Grounds`); (b) `freeSlot_kernel_write` (the arrival kernel state is `write3Eff` of these
  leaves, every one `Init` with no hypothesis on its prior state, `Moved → Init` included; nothing else
  changes); (c) `freeSlot_abstract_update` (slot free, generation + 1, `A` and `D` unchanged: no memory
  right added; the metadata leaves of the updated pool are the written leaves). (c) holds at the level of
  leaf identity and initialization only: `S3` has no value component (§38). Also
  `freeSlot_meta_disjoint` (the write does not touch the freed entry) and the conforming case
  `Witness.meta_write_not_identity` (accepted `freeSlot` on a pool value with a `Moved` leaf, which
  becomes `Init`).
- Q17 (validated 2026-11-06), `Access.transfer_source_q17`: after an accepted `transfer` from a reachable
  state, for every authority `g` grounding the right over the source, (a) every active authority covering a
  source leaf is in `RightChain g`; (b) as restated by the owner on 2026-11-06: every read of a source leaf
  is rejected (through every authority), every access through a strict ancestor of `g` is rejected, and a
  write through `g` itself is permitted, a re-initialization (positive witness
  `TransferSourceWitness.write_through_ground_accepted`).
- §63.4 redundancy, `Access.reachable_noOutsideDerived_of_right`: on reachable states the `Modify` right over
  the source (§63.1) implies the derived-outside check of §63.4, which therefore never rejects a `transfer`
  by itself there; the clause is kept.
- StaticsOK (a): `Access.StaticsConf.exists_renumber` (every declaration conforming to §47/§49, with no
  order between identifiers, has a consistent renumbering, field order kept (§63.2), satisfying
  `StaticsOK`); `StaticsConf.of_staticsOK` (converse).
- StaticsOK (b), kernel bisimulation (`MemoryModel/Access/Rename/*`): for two `StaticsOK` numberings of
  one declaration related by a consistent renaming (`Renumbered`: parents, owners, kinds, initial states and
  field order kept), every run of O1–O16 has the same verdicts with renamed arguments and the reached
  states correspond (`Renumbered.run`, `Renumbered.run_back`; per operation `op_corr`, `ok`/`reject`/`fail`
  alike); reachability corresponds both ways (`Renumbered.reachable`, `Renumbered.reachable_back`); `KInv`
  and `I5` transfer (`Sim.kinv`, `Sim.i5`), so the properties proved on reachable states are the same for
  both numberings (`Renumbered.properties`, with `DDSound` invariant). Any two numberings obtained by (a)
  are so related (`renumber_renumbered`). States correspond up to permutation of authority footprints,
  anchor lists and pinned-leaf lists (§42, §44: sets); `K` is renamed (`K.rename`; `FreeCompat`'s `auth`,
  opaque by §70.2, and the obligation identities of `ExternalDone`, §75, are not), under `KExt`
  (open point 4).
- Q7: `Arena.resetNoDeps_of_noCover` (§78.3 from §78.2 and I3), `Arena.reset_iff_derive_release` (`reset` iff
  `derive` then `release`, both directions, `ok` and `reject`).
- B#45: `Access.pin_unpinEff_iff` (`unpin` ends the designated obligation only), `Access.reachable_i5`,
  `Refinement.pinned_address_stable_reachable`, corpus case `Corpus.MM3H.B45`.

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.OpsTransfer
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.OpsFrames
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.OpsEndFree
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.Invariants
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.Init

/-!
# Renaming of identities: the kernel bisimulation

Assembly of the renaming bisimulation of the access kernel for
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` §49, last paragraph: per operation O1–O16
(§58, §60–§75), per run (§57, §58), on reachable states (§57) from the initial states of two
`StaticsOK` numberings of one declaration (§47; §63.2), and the transfer of `KInv`, `I5` (§57)
and `DDSound` (§80). Owner decision of 2026-11-06 on `StaticsOK`, point (b); `KExt` is the
owner-accepted hypothesis on `Satisfiable` (§71). Any two numberings given by point (a)
(`StaticsConf.exists_renumber`) are related (`renumber_renumbered`).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename

variable {π α : Ren} {s s' t t' : S3} {k : K}

/-! ## One operation (§58, §60–§75) -/

/-- Every operation O1–O16 and its renamed arguments have corresponding outcomes on related
states (§58, §60–§75; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem op_corr (hk : KExt k) (hS : Sim π α s s') (op : KernelOp) :
    StepCorr π α (op.Step k s) ((op.ren π α).Step (k.rename π α) s') := by
  cases op with
    have hxl : x < σ₁.length := hl₁ ▸ hlen ▸ lt_of_staticParent hx
    have hyl : y < σ₁.length := hl₁ ▸ hlen ▸ lt_of_staticParent hy
    have hx0 : σ₁[x] < C.length := (hmem hp₁ _).1 (List.getElem_mem hxl)
    have hy0 : σ₁[y] < C.length := (hmem hp₁ _).1 (List.getElem_mem hyl)
    rw [renumber_parent hp₁ hxl] at hx
    rw [renumber_parent hp₁ hyl] at hy
    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 hx
    obtain ⟨b, hb, hab⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 hy
    have hab : b = a := hinj hp₁ b a (hC.parent_lt _ _ hb) (hC.parent_lt _ _ ha) hab
    subst hab
    have ex : σ₁.idxOf σ₁[x] = x := idxOf_getElem hp₁ hxl
    have ey : σ₁.idxOf σ₁[y] = y := idxOf_getElem hp₁ hyl
    have hlt : σ₁[x] < σ₁[y] := by
      rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy σ₁[x] σ₁[y] with h | h | h
      · exact h
      · rw [← ex, ← ey, h] at hxy; exact absurd hxy (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
      · have := hc₁.field_order _ _ _ hb ha h
        rw [ex, ey] at this; omega
    have := hc₂.field_order _ _ _ ha hb hlt
    rw [← ex, ← ey, hτidx, hτidx]
    exact this
  refine ⟨τ, ⟨hτ, ⟨fun x hx => renumber_entry hτ hx, hfo⟩, hok₁, heq ▸ hok₂⟩, heq⟩

/-! ## Non-vacuity (§47, §48, §57, §58; §49, last paragraph) -/

namespace MainExamples

open Examples InitExamples

/-- `KExt` is satisfiable: `K0.Satisfiable` is constantly true (§48, §71). -/
theorem k0_ext : KExt K0 := fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => trivial

/-- A run of `n1` (§47) with an accepted `pin` and a rejected `unpin` (§74, §75) has the renamed
run with the same verdicts on the renumbering `[3, 0, 1, 2]` of `n1` (§49, last paragraph). -/
example : ∃ u', Run (K0.rename n1_renumbered.π n1_renumbered.α)
    (S3.init (renumber [3, 0, 1, 2] n1))
    ([KernelOp.pin 1, .unpin 1].map (KernelOp.ren n1_renumbered.π n1_renumbered.α))
    [.ok (), .reject] u' ∧ Sim n1_renumbered.π n1_renumbered.α (pinEff (S3.init n1) 1) u' :=
  n1_renumbered.run k0_ext
    (.ok (show PinStep 1 (S3.init n1) (.ok (pinEff (S3.init n1) 1)) from .ok (by decide))
      (.reject (show UnpinStep K0 1 (pinEff (S3.init n1) 1) .reject from .reject (by decide))
        .nil))

end MainExamples

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename

/-- Shape of the locals of `enterFrame` (§72) and of an allocation (§71.1): each element is an
optional structural parent (a place index) and a `kind`. Every element is owned by the holder
receiving the shape. -/
abbrev LocalShape := List (Option Nat × Nat)

/-- External contract `K` (§48, §80): `DeclaredDisjoint` on regions (§23, §61.3);
`SharedMutable` and `Pinned` on leaves (§68.1, §63.5); `ExternalDone` on dynamic pinning
obligations, by identity (§75); `Deallocable` on places (§70.2); `FreeCompat place auth` (§70.2);
`Satisfiable provider shape s` (§71). Obligations of `K` are hypotheses of theorems, never
fields. -/
structure K where
  DeclaredDisjoint : List Nat → List Nat → Prop
  SharedMutable : Nat → Prop
  Pinned : Nat → Prop
  ExternalDone : Nat → Prop
  Deallocable : Nat → Prop
  FreeCompat : Nat → Nat → Prop
  Satisfiable : Nat → LocalShape → S3 → Prop

/-- `DDSound(K)` (§80, §23): no declared disjointness relates two regions sharing a leaf. -/
def DDSound (k : K) : Prop := ∀ r r', k.DeclaredDisjoint r r' → ∀ l ∈ r, l ∉ r'

/-- `origin` link of authority `i` (§42). -/
def S3.org (s : S3) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (s.A[i]?).bind (·.origin)

/-- Strict ancestors of authority `i` along its origin chain (§42, §43). -/
def S3.ancs (s : S3) (i : Nat) : List Nat := chain s.org i

/-- Effective anchor of `x` (§44): the root reached along its origin chain, the last element of
`x :: s.ancs x`. -/
def S3.effAnchor (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Nat := (s.ancs x).getLastD x

/-- Active authority (§42); as an anchor, a valid anchor (§44). -/
def S3.Active (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Prop := ∃ y, s.A[x]? = some y ∧ y.active = true

/-- Decidability of `S3.Active` (§42, §44). -/
instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Decidable (s.Active x) :=
  match h : s.A[x]? with
  | some y => if hy : y.active = true then isTrue ⟨y, h, hy⟩
    else isFalse fun ⟨y', h', hy'⟩ => by rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact hy hy'
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨_, h', _⟩ => by rw [h] at h'; cases h'

/-- Current frame, the top of the stack (§39). -/
def S3.top (s : S3) : Nat := s.F.headD 0
